SECTION IV - THE PROBABLE IMPACT OF THE PROPOSED ACTION ON THE ENVIRONMENT
Probable Impacts During the Construction Period
4.01 Air Quality. A temporary degradation of air quality in the immediate area of the construction site is to be expected. The problem should not be serious and will consist primarily of dust and exhaust fumes generated by heavy construction equipment. The dust problem will be controlled to a large extent by keeping haul roads watered to minimize dust. No other or unusual air contaminants are expected to be produced in significant quantities during construction of the proposed project.
4.02 Water Quality. During construction of the proposed hydropower facilities, a temporary degradation of water quality below Amistad Reservoir can be expected. This will occur primarily as a result of the construction and removal of a cofferdam which will be required for construction of the powerhouse. This degradation of water quality will be the result of additional suspended solids introduced into the river as a result of working in the streambed. After completion of the cofferdam, water quality impacts will probably be minimal.
4.03 Noise. As typical of any construction project, there will be noise levels somewhat higher than background or normal conditions before and after construction; however, no unusual noise levels are anticipated. The location of the construction site will help prevent bothersome noise levels from reaching local residents because of its distance from them. The site is located in the riverbed at the foot of the dam and is somewhat lower than the surrounding area which should help muffle the noise.
4.04 Sanitation at the Site. Any construction involves the production of waste materials which must be disposed of in some manner. The collection and proper disposal of such waste will be required of the contractor by the project specifications. No significant impacts are envisioned as a result of the handling and disposal of these wastes.
4.05 Hazardous Materials. Hazardous materials used at the construction site should consist primarily of petrochemical products used in fueling and maintaining the equipment necessary in the construction of the powerhouse. Contract requirements will specify that these materials be stored according to accepted standards of safety. No other hazardous materials such as pesticides, herbicides, or explosives are expected to be maintained onsite at this time. No significant impacts are anticipated from hazardous materials.
4.06 Land Features and Uses. Facilities that are constructed will require the consignment of land for the life of the facility. Although the facilities will occupy a small area which has been previously excavated, their presence would preempt other uses however limited they may be. There will be a minor secondary impact from the probable line conversion from Central Power and Light's facilities into the dam and substation. No new transmission line will be constructed.
4.07 Geologic Resource. The primary impact upon economic geology will be the irretrievable commitment of mineral resources utilized in the construction of project facilities. This effect is not considered a significant impact, but the utilization of mineral resources for this project would preclude its availability for other projects.
